points: After the $300 million sale of Cboe Australia and Canada, upcoming reports should show a simpler, higher-margin business mix; if U.S. options and derivatives keep growing, the lost international revenue becomes less important.
The CEDX wind-down already happened in February 2026, so year-over-year comparisons in the next few quarters will lap that revenue hole and any new product can more easily show net growth.
The 20% workforce reduction is already baked into costs, so the next print and the quarters after will test whether cost discipline can hold operating margins above 65% even if revenue growth cools.

The May 2026 extended trading session for multi-listed equity options is now live; upcoming volume data will reveal whether it brings genuinely new activity or merely shifts trades from regular hours.

The April 2026 rules allowing options on multi-crypto trusts give Cboe a new product avenue; the next 12 months will show whether it can generate more than $50 million in incremental revenue, which the thesis needs.
The proposed Options Regulatory Fee is a live risk; if it is implemented and cuts revenue by more than 5%, it would break the margin-expansion case, so regulatory updates through 2027 matter.

MSCI's October 20 report is the nearest peer print and can act as a read on data and index demand; strength would support the broader exchange/data theme, while weakness could weigh on Cboe's valuation.
A sustained options volume decline of more than 10% year over year would invalidate the core long thesis, making the next few quarters' volume trends the key numbers to watch.
